review_scope: Exact Python distribution identities and declared licenses in both official ComfyUI v0.30.0 Windows NVIDIA portable assets, verified against the downloaded payloads rather than their indexes alone.

asset_evidence.method: Immutable release metadata plus the complete payloads: both assets were downloaded, their SHA-256 computed over the whole file, and their dist-info identities, METADATA and bundled license bodies read from the archives themselves. The embedded CPython version was read from the python DLL version resource rather than by executing it.

vulnerability_audit.requirements_source: Exact dist-info identities from both downloaded portable archives; CUDA local version suffixes were normalized only for advisory lookup.

change_from_previous_release.note: The distribution set is identical in membership and count; 23 pinned versions moved. torch 2.13.0, torchaudio, torchvision, Pillow and setuptools are unchanged, so the runtime probe's package expectations carry over and only its ComfyUI version moves. The frontend package moved 1.45.21 to 1.47.11, which is a certification input rather than a dependency fact.

non_dist_info_components.name: CPython Windows embeddable security overlay
non_dist_info_components.license: Python-2.0; bundled third-party notices retained in LICENSE.txt

limitations: This is a point-in-time technical inventory and vulnerability review, not legal advice or final legal approval.
License bodies were read where declared metadata carried no SPDX expression; the remaining bundled notices are indexed by path rather than hashed individually.

The CUDA 12.6 tier remains blocked: this release still embeds CPython 3.12.10, and no patched official Windows 3.12 binary exists. It is inventoried here so the manifest stays coherent, not to enable it.
An isolated runtime version and import probe still has to run against a provisioned tree before this release can be activated, and provisioning is held.
